newsitem.title: USA: Pratt expects FTC approval of engine joint venture.
newsitem.headline: Pratt expects FTC approval of engine joint venture.

text.p: A Pratt & Whitney spokesman said Monday the company expected the Federal Trade Commission (FTC) to approve its joint venture with General Electric Co. to build longer-range Boeing Co. 747 engines.
"We expect it to be approved and we expect it to move forward," Mark Sullivan, a Pratt spokesman, told Reuters.

The FTC is reviewing whether the partnership between Pratt - a unit of United Technologies Corp. - and GE violates federal antitrust laws, hurts consumers or reduces U.S. exports. "We consider this a routine review of this alliance," said Sullivan.
"We intend to compete very vigorously in this market as a joint venture," he said.
The new engines under development are intended to power larger and longer-range models of the 747.
